coverageNote: Audited all 32 current Markdown sources in six units: the five 08.01-08.05 sub-domain folders and the root unit containing 08.06-08.08 plus the domain index and cross-cuts. No path under .memory/wiki/specs/audits/ was read.

findings.claim: Open decisions on timing mode, telemetry retention and consent, threshold sourcing, and commercial handling list an owner and destination but omit both a deadline and the decision blocked.

evidence.excerpt: Q-02 asks whether the verdict is worth building and lists only User and MoSCoW.
Q-02 asks whether per-pair telemetry persists and for how long, with only User and /create-prd-security.
Q-01 asks where instrument-pair thresholds come from, with only User + Agent and /create-prd-compile.
Q-01 asks whether to commit to symmetric, conductor, or both timing models, with only User and /create-prd.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose the timing model, threshold table, data-use consent, and paid-session behavior without knowing which product decision must be resolved first.
findings.failureScenario: Different room implementations select incompatible timing modes or expose and retain home-network diagnostics under incompatible consent rules.

findings.claim: Location disclosure, availability semantics, correction error trade-offs, history retention, and stale-predicate behavior are open without a deadline or an explicit blocked decision.

evidence.excerpt: Q-01 asks who can see a musician's location and at what precision, with only User and /create-prd-security.
Q-01 asks the owner to choose false-shrink versus false-grow behavior, with only User and /create-prd.
Q-02 asks consumers' stale-predicate obligation, with only Agent and /create-prd-architecture.
Whether a materially shrunk radius notifies the user remains PENDING.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must invent location visibility, confidence-result consequences, stale-result handling, and whether degraded reach is surfaced to the affected person.
findings.failureScenario: The map and consumer filters can leak location or remove people from searches with inconsistent notices and retention behavior.

findings.claim: The route-aware correction's core arbitration behavior is explicitly undecided: it lacks the confidence model, sample threshold, decay policy, and per-route versus per-peer scope.

evidence.excerpt: [PARTIAL] — the arbitration rule is the substance of this feature and is genuinely undecided.
The actual confidence model, sample thresholds, decay rate, and per-route or per-peer correction are PENDING.
The correction needs a confidence model, not a last-value-wins rule.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose the model that determines when a person's discovery radius moves and how long a bad probe affects it.
findings.failureScenario: A transient probe can arbitrarily shrink a user's reach, while another implementation uses a different aggregation rule and presents conflicting map and filter results.

findings.claim: Security, access, feedback, playback-context, and speculative-product decisions are open without a deadline or a documented blocked decision; the live-feedback batching policy is also left pending outside the question table.

evidence.excerpt: Q-02 asks whether watermarking or DRM-grade controls are needed, with only User and /create-prd-security.
Q-01 leaves invite-link hardening unresolved with only User and /create-prd-security.
Q-01 asks whether commenting is a separate grant from listening, with only User and /create-prd-security.
Q-01 asks whether Monitoring Trust is a real product, with only User and /create-prd.
High note volume needs collapsing or batching, but the behavior is PENDING.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide who can annotate unreleased material, how links are hardened, how critique reaches performers, and how a live note flood is controlled.
findings.failureScenario: A listener may gain unintended comment access or overwhelm a producer during a take, while unreleased audio uses inconsistent link and retention protections.

findings.claim: The cue-mix viability, local-source delay choice, hardware-talkback interoperability, latching behavior, and monitoring-profile ownership decisions lack deadlines and stated blocked decisions.

evidence.excerpt: Q-01 asks whether a networked cue mix can exist properly, with only Agent and /create-prd.
Q-01 leaves the shared talkback and performance microphone path unresolved.
Q-02 leaves the local-source delay trade-off unresolved, with only Agent and /create-prd.
Q-01 leaves the monitoring-profile and playback-context entity boundary unresolved.
Whether a portable minimal-ducking preference can be overridden remains PARTIAL and PENDING.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether the feature is viable, which authority overrides personal monitoring preferences, and how to protect capture when physical and platform talkback share hardware.
findings.failureScenario: Performers can receive incompatible cue timing or an unmodeled authority override, while a shared microphone path can contaminate a keeper take.

findings.claim: Storage, consent, post-upload withdrawal, attribution accountability, witness retention, alignment guarantees, flag visibility, and provenance disclosure decisions are open without a deadline or a documented blocked decision.

evidence.excerpt: Q-03 asks who consents to recording and when, with only User and /create-prd-security.
Q-02 asks whether a take can be withdrawn after upload, with only User and /create-prd.
Q-04 asks whether the timeline can be absolute or only relative, with only Agent and /create-prd-architecture.
Q-01 asks whether flags are private or shared, with only User and /create-prd.
Q-02 leaves the legal basis and retention limit for recording unresolved.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose consent and retention rules, storage and withdrawal behavior, evidence disclosure, timeline guarantees, and how personal contribution signals are exposed.
findings.failureScenario: A capture system can retain or delete evidence under incompatible rules, misstate a timeline guarantee, or expose contribution data before its authority and consent model exist.

findings.claim: Manual highlighting requires a retrospective region but defines neither its duration nor a user-selection policy.

evidence.excerpt: A late flag must anchor to a window before the gesture, but no window bounds are specified.
The annotation calls a retrospective window the feature but gives only a non-normative last-30-seconds example.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose how much prior audio a flag captures and whether the player can change that range.
findings.failureScenario: A flag can omit the moment a musician intended to preserve or produce an impractically large review region.

findings.claim: Domain-level infrastructure, domain-folding, performance, consent, pre-flight, commercial-hold, authority-succession, and merge questions list owners and stages but omit deadlines and stated blocked decisions.

evidence.excerpt: Q-03 asks whether to accept dedicated media infrastructure or reduce the domain, with only User and /create-prd-stack.
Q-01 asks whether paid bookings can require pre-flight and its commercial consequence, with only User and /create-prd.
Q-02 asks for acceptable residual timing error per instrument, with only User + Agent and /create-prd-compile.
Q-01 leaves the paid-session hold ceiling and meter behavior unresolved, with only User and /create-prd.
CX-11 remains Deferred to Step 5 despite Step 5 having completed.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must decide if required media infrastructure exists, when a result becomes stale, how long a paid session waits, who succeeds a disconnected producer, and whether duplicated interactions are one object.
findings.failureScenario: The product can ship conflicting commercial, authority, and provenance behavior across live and overdub flows because no decision has a completion commitment.

findings.claim: The domain index still treats Overdub provenance as equivalent to observed live-session provenance, while the current Overdub and attendance specs require a lower delivery-based grade.

evidence.excerpt: D-04 says the platform observes who played what and that 08.05.04 ships with any session mechanism, including Overdub.
D-05 says Overdub carries the provenance intact.
Overdub is explicitly corrected to delivery-certainty, not performance-certainty.
An overdub record has delivery-certainty and becomes observed-playing only for segments a live witness observed.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether an overdub row is emitted as observed playing or as delivered by, and what evidence grade Credits receives.
findings.failureScenario: An uploaded or ghost-played pass can be labeled as direct observation of a human performance, overstating credit evidence and creating a rights-dispute risk.

findings.claim: Interruption handling leaves the take lifecycle open even though capture and alignment specify one take containing timestamped segments and preserved gaps.

evidence.excerpt: Q-03 still asks whether an interruption splits a take or continues it as one.
An interrupted recording resumes inside one take as segments with session-relative timestamps and an explicit gap marker.
D-11 resolves fragments as independently aligned with preserved gaps and inherited drift within a track.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether reconnect creates a new take identity or appends a segment to the existing take.
findings.failureScenario: Upload, alignment, attendance, and user-facing session history can disagree about how many takes exist after a reconnect.

findings.claim: Overdub says an interrupted upload persists only until request expiry but also requires late takes to be accepted and aligned; the state of a queued local pass at expiry is unspecified.

evidence.excerpt: An interrupted upload persists until the request expires.
After the deadline passes, the request becomes expired when nothing was delivered.
A player delivering after the deadline is accepted and aligned; 08 does not enforce commercial deadlines.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether a locally queued pass is preserved and resumable, canceled, or manually recoverable after expiry.
findings.failureScenario: A recoverable late pass is discarded by one client, while another uploads it and creates inconsistent asset, payment, and dispute records.

findings.claim: The domain cross-cut describes no-reference and no-witness handling as correlation or timestamp alignment, but the alignment feature says raw distributed tracks cannot correlate and R3 must be published as unaligned.

evidence.excerpt: If the reference is absent and R2 was not pre-armed, alignment degrades to correlation or timestamp.
R3 cannot measure drift and cannot produce an aligned result.
Distributed raw tracks have no shared acoustic content, so track-to-track correlation is structurally impossible.

findings.forcedInvention: An implementer must choose whether to fabricate an aligned result from timestamps, attempt impossible raw-track correlation, or publish an unaligned placement hint.
findings.failureScenario: A session without a recorded reference receives a misleading low-confidence alignment instead of an explicit unaligned result, corrupting a multitrack silently.
